title: Pterygium removal
what: The surgeon removes a growth of tissue that spreads onto the cornea. Usually a small piece of your own eye tissue is placed over that spot.
why: When the growth gets bigger, blocks your vision, causes irritation, or bothers you by how it looks.
duration: surgery usually takes 30 to 60 minutes; you usually go home the same day
tell_doctor: If you take blood thinners. The doctor will decide what to do
If you have diabetes or high blood pressure
If you had surgery on this eye before

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Usually blood tests and an exam are needed. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your medicines on your own. Tell the doctor.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: Have someone take you home. You cannot drive.

prepare.title: Makeup
prepare.text: No makeup on the day of surgery.

steps: Numbing drops are put in your eye, sometimes with an injection near the eye
A small device holds your eyelids open
The surgeon separates and removes the growth
A piece of your own tissue is stitched or glued over the spot
Your eye is covered with a patch
feel: During surgery, you feel pressure but not pain
For a few days, it feels like sand in the eye, with stinging and watering
Redness of the eye lasts a few weeks
after: Use the drops exactly as the doctor said
Checkups as the doctor plans. Stitches are removed or dissolve on their own
Protect your eyes from the sun. This lowers the risk of the growth coming back
red_flags: Severe pain that keeps getting worse
A stitch came apart or the tissue piece moved

faq.a: Yes, sometimes. The tissue graft and sun protection lower this risk.

faq.q: Do I have to have surgery?
faq.a: A small growth is often just watched. Surgery is advised if it grows or gets in the way.

reminders.text: Eye surgery tomorrow. Bring sunglasses and arrange for someone to take you home.
